subject: reasoning
question: Six people, Q, R, S, T, U and Y, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only one person sits between Q and Y when counted from the left of Y. Y sits third to the left of R. U sits to the immediate right of Y. S is not an immediate neighbour of Y . How many people sit between S and T when counted from the right of S?
solution:
**Given: **Six people, Q, R, S, T, U and Y, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order).

Only one person sits between Q and Y when counted from the left of Y. Y sits third to the left of R.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9ec43e467af2e13a8211174b291b0949c5ffcc0123d98e04875e036b250cd6f4.png] 

U sits to the immediate right of Y. S is not an immediate neighbour of Y .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8a6c153d789f081bb0c6113da9a18d1c6315c655b4092745f301ce4ff962a2b2.png] 

Thus, Only two people sit between S and T when counted from the right of S.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**
